description: Causal chains that move German (and EU) construction prices. Each link is a hypothesis with a mechanism and the free data that can test it; it becomes a training edge only when an official accounting source (input-output table, index weights) or a test in scripts/ops/estimate_links.py supports it. Node references: sector:<code> and commodity:<slug> exist in config/sectors.json; new:<id> nodes are listed under new_nodes with the source that would measure them. Status: in_store (both ends measured), tested_supported / tested_not_supported (see reports/graph-links-latest.json), needs_data.

eu_carbon_price.label: EU ETS allowance price (EUR/t CO2)
eu_carbon_price.source: EEX primary auction results (daily, free download) or ICAP allowance price explorer

de_fuel_co2_price.label: German fuel CO2 price (BEHG fixed price / corridor)

cbam_phase_in.label: Share of CBAM goods' emissions charged (free allocation phase-out)

truck_toll_co2.label: Truck toll CO2 surcharge (EUR/t CO2, since 2023-12-01)

eur_usd.label: EUR/USD exchange rate
eur_usd.source: ECB EXR monthly average (EXR.M.USD.EUR.SP00.A, in store)

import_prices.label: Import prices of construction materials
import_prices.source: Destatis 61411 import price indices by GP2019 product

coal_generation.label: Hard coal and lignite power generation (GWh)
coal_generation.source: SMARD generation data (CC BY 4.0; source disabled until the date fix is retracted)

minimum_wage.label: Statutory and construction minimum wages
minimum_wage.source: MiLoG section 1, MiLoV4, MiLoV5 via LAW_PARAMETERS (series POLICY|DE|MiLoG|minimum_wage, 2023-2027)

construction_employment.label: Persons employed in main construction trade

civil_engineering_prices.label: Road and civil engineering price indices

renovation_subsidy.label: Federal efficient-building subsidy (BEG) rates and stops
renovation_subsidy.source: BEG funding guidelines (Bundesanzeiger) as a dated policy series

efficiency_standard.label: Statutory energy standard for new buildings
efficiency_standard.source: GEG (ingested) and EPBD (ingested) as a dated policy series

vat_rate.label: German VAT rate
vat_rate.source: UStG section 12 (in store as model input)

road_freight_prices.label: Road freight producer prices
road_freight_prices.source: Destatis 61311 service producer prices (freight transport by road)

cross_border_supply.label: Imports of materials by origin country
cross_border_supply.source: Eurostat FIGARO naio_10_fcp_ip1-ip4 (FLOWS_TO with scope origin>dest, 2010-2024)

chains.label: Energy -> energy-intensive materials -> trades -> building price
chains.why: Cement, lime, bricks, glass, plasterboard and steel are energy-intensive; their price passes to the trades that use them, weighted by the official trade weights.

links.mechanism: electric arc furnaces make rebar from scrap

links.note: not supported in 2005-2026 quarterly data; labour and the common trend dominate

links.mechanism: official weight 17.3% of the new-home index

chains.label: Carbon prices -> cement, lime, steel, glass; fuel CO2 price -> diesel and heating
chains.why: ETS sectors pay for emissions above free allocation; CBAM phases free allocation out from 2026 and charges imports; BEHG prices fuels outside the ETS.

links.mechanism: about 0.6 t CO2 per t clinker; cost above free allocation
scales how much of the carbon price CBAM goods actually pay (2026 2.5% -> 2034 100%)
certificate cost on imported cement, steel, aluminium
about 2.65 kg CO2 per litre diesel
CO2 surcharge on truck toll since 2023-12-01

chains.label: World commodity prices and the dollar -> imported inputs -> German producer prices
chains.why: Oil, ore, aluminium, copper and timber are priced in dollars on world markets; German producer prices follow with a lag.

links.note: world price stored; no German price series long enough for the target
world price stored; no German price series long enough for the target

links.mechanism: world aluminium price to German producer price
links.note: world price stored; no German price series long enough for the target

links.mechanism: titanium-zinc sheet for roofs and gutters
copper pipes in water and heating installations

chains.label: Wage agreements and minimum wages -> labour cost -> trades
chains.why: Labour is about 40-50% of trade prices; agreed wage rises are announced months ahead, which makes them a leading indicator.

links.mechanism: labour share in the input-output table
tight labour market raises wage drift

chains.label: Interest rates -> mortgages -> permits -> orders -> backlog -> margins -> prices
chains.why: Prices include a margin that follows demand; rate rises cut permits and orders a year later and builders' price expectations turn.

links.mechanism: mortgage rates set demand for new homes (via permits and orders)
capacity exit after a demand fall

chains.label: Public investment -> civil engineering orders -> civil engineering prices
chains.why: The 2025 infrastructure fund and municipal budgets drive road and rail work, which competes with housing for firms and materials.

chains.label: Heating law and subsidies -> heat pump demand -> heating trade prices
chains.why: GEG 2024 (65% renewable heating) and BEG subsidy changes moved heat pump demand sharply in 2023-2024.

links.mechanism: subsidy raises demand and lets suppliers raise prices

chains.label: Energy standards -> more material per m2 -> cost per m2 (not the price index)
chains.why: Price indices hold quality fixed, so a stricter standard shows up in cost per square metre (permit-stage planned cost), not in the index. Training must use the right label for this chain.

links.mechanism: planned cost per m2 in building permits (31111-0020, in store)

chains.label: Coal phase-out -> less flue-gas gypsum -> plasterboard prices
chains.why: About half of German gypsum came from coal plant desulphurisation; the coal exit (KVBG) shrinks that supply and shifts it to quarried or recycled gypsum.

chains.label: Diesel, toll and drivers -> freight -> delivered bulk materials
chains.why: Sand, gravel and ready-mixed concrete are heavy and cheap per tonne, so transport is a large share of their delivered price.

chains.label: VAT -> price including VAT
chains.why: The forecast target includes VAT; the 2007 rise and the 2020 cut are mechanical jumps.

links.mechanism: price incl. VAT = price excl. VAT x (1 + rate)

chains.label: Neighbouring countries' material prices -> German import prices -> German producer prices
chains.why: Cement, steel and timber trade across borders (Poland, Czechia, Austria, Benelux); a shock in one country's materials reaches others through trade shares.

links.mechanism: import shares from FIGARO weight the partner countries' producer prices (EU panel, in store)
links.note: 2026-10-21: German wood/mineral/metal producer prices follow EU producer prices (pass-through ~1), but FIGARO import weights fit no better than equal weights: European co-movement, not trade transmission at this level.

not_nodes.events: Covid, the war in Ukraine, the 2021 floods and similar one-off events are dated annotations, not training nodes: each happened once, and their effect enters through measured channels (energy, materials, surveys). Policy changes that recur become numeric policy series instead (new_nodes with 'policy series' in the source).
